org.nasdanika.models.product-management:.documentation: Legacy modernization is the process of re-binding decisions that earlier teams already bound - in older languages, against older requirements, often with the original intent now lost across generations of owners and maintainers. This model treats that work as a product rather than a one-off migration: the personas below carry distinct, frequently competing concerns, and the capabilities exist to serve those concerns explicitly rather than by informal consensus. The aim is to preserve business intent while replacing the runtime, surfacing trade-offs between stakeholders as deliberate choices instead of side effects of technical decisions.
org.nasdanika.models.product-management:.name: Legacy Modernization

personas.documentation: Have knowledge of business logic and edge cases. In many cases of legacy modernization such knowledge is lost because the system lived through multiple generations of business owners, maintainers and other personals.
personas.name: Business Owners

concerns.documentation:
The modernized system must produce the same outputs for the same inputs as the legacy system - including edge cases and undocumented behavior. Because business logic accreted across generations of owners and maintainers and is often no longer written down anywhere, parity is verified mechanically against captured legacy behavior rather than against specs that may not exist.
Phase 1 Direct Semantic Execution preserves legacy semantics exactly, so parity is structural rather than interpretive.
concerns.name: Behaviorial parity

concerns.documentation: Service levels the business currently depends on - throughput, latency, availability, batch completion windows - must hold through and after migration. Modernization changes the runtime, not the commitments made to downstream consumers, so existing SLAs are carried into the target as constraints rather than renegotiated by the migration.
concerns.name: SLA continuity

personas.documentation: Owns the target state. Concerned that each migrated unit aligns with the target reference architecture and that the modernization adds the minimum bespoke surface area needed - moving the estate toward a deliberate destination, not just off the legacy stack.
personas.name: Enterprise Architecture

concerns.documentation: Each modernized deployment unit should move the estate toward the target reference architecture, not merely off the legacy stack. Per-unit approach selection is made explicit through structured decision analysis so individual migration choices compose into the intended end state instead of drifting into incidental, comfort-driven outcomes.
concerns.name: Strategic direction

concerns.documentation: Remove the hard dependency on the legacy vendor's proprietary runtime and formats. Phase 1 (DSE) achieves this first by executing legacy artifacts AS-IS on an owned model-driven engine - a defensible end state on its own and a precondition for unconstrained Phase 2 modernization. Keeping bespoke surface area in the target minimal prevents trading one form of lock-in for another.
concerns.name: Vendor independence

personas.documentation: Supports the system in production, before and after cutover. Concerned with retaining observability, troubleshooting access, and valid runbooks, so the modernized system is no harder to keep running than the one it replaces.
personas.name: Operations/SRE

concerns.documentation: Production troubleshooting access and telemetry available on the legacy system must remain available on the modernized one. Model-based telemetry emits traces tagged by model element URI, giving operators unified troubleshooting across the model and the running system.
concerns.name: Observability continuity

concerns.documentation: Existing operational procedures and on-call runbooks must remain valid or be regenerated alongside the migration, so the system stays supportable in production from cutover onward.
concerns.name: Runbook continuity

personas.documentation: Owns control posture and compliance. Concerned that controls have demonstrable equivalents post-migration, that the transition itself is auditable, and that no control gaps open during phased cutover.
personas.name: Security & Risk

concerns.documentation: Security and compliance controls present in the legacy system must have demonstrable equivalents post-migration, with no weakening of posture introduced by the runtime change.
concerns.name: Control posture equivalence

concerns.documentation: The migration itself must be auditable - what was translated, how, and verified against what - and existing audit trails (e.g., for SOX) must survive the transition rather than be broken by it.
concerns.name: Audit trail through transition

concerns.documentation: Phased cutover must avoid windows where a control present in the legacy system is absent in the target.
concerns.name: No control gaps during cutover

personas.documentation: Owns timeline and budget. Concerned with time-to-value, visible incremental progress, and predictable milestones - which is why early removal of the legacy runtime dependency (Phase 1) matters more than a distant big-bang finish.
personas.name: Delivery Management

concerns.documentation: Deliver removal of the legacy runtime dependency early (Phase 1) to realize value and de-risk before the longer Phase 2 work, rather than waiting on a single large rewrite.
concerns.name: Time-to-value

concerns.documentation: Per-deployment-unit phasing produces visible, incremental progress and predictable milestones instead of a big-bang schedule with a single uncertain finish.
concerns.name: Predictable milestones

personas.documentation: Will own and evolve the system once the migration team is gone. Concerned that behavior is captured in a model with regression coverage rather than residing in people's heads, so the system can be changed safely and traceably after cutover.
personas.name: Maintainers

concerns.documentation: After cutover, maintainers must be able to change the system with confidence. Because behavior is captured in a model with regression coverage and the runtime is owned rather than vendor-controlled, changes can be validated against preserved semantics — turning a system whose logic lived in people's heads into one that can be evolved with traceability.
concerns.name: Ability to evolve safely post-migration

capabilities.documentation: Legacy artifacts may require legacy editors/viewers which will be gone post-migration. It is important to have documentation of the system as it was. For a small system it can be done by taking screenshots. For a system of non-trivial size it might be more efficient to write a documentation generator.
capabilities.name: Documentation generator
